Proposal: Conversion of an existing 30-foot diameter (approximately 660 sq ft) lattice yurt into low-impact guest quarters for short-term experiential lodging as part of the approved agritourism farm stay operation.
Scope of Work:
The project consists of interior modifications and utility improvements to the existing yurt structure to create basic guest quarters (no full kitchen). All work will be performed by the owner-builder.
Proposed Improvements:

Construction of a single wet-wall for utilities and a small framed bathroom enclosure.
Installation of a washer/dryer (propane) supplied by Ferrell Gas.
Rough-in and finish plumbing for a shower, bathroom sink, and laundry hookups.
Installation of a tankless propane water heater and direct-vent propane heater.
Rough-in and finish electrical work including outlets, lighting, and wiring for small loads (portable swamp cooler, small kitchen appliances, and fan).
Installation of a ground-mounted off-grid solar system with battery storage to serve the electrical needs of the guest quarters.
Connection of a new water line from the existing city water line currently serving the main residence to the yurt.
Wastewater management will be provided by either a compost toilet with graywater system (shower, sink, and laundry to mulch basin) or a new onsite wastewater treatment system (OWTS/septic).

The yurt will function as short-term guest quarters supporting the regenerative farm’s agritourism activities. Guests will have access to the farm’s u-pick orchard and livestock operations for educational and immersive experiences. The structure will remain under 1,000 sq ft and will not include a full kitchen.
